change_log.summary: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia expanded to more cities/energy sites; Yemen border restricted zone widened
change_log.detail: FCDO advice updated 20 Sep 2026: Houthi missile/drone attacks since mid-July 2026 now cited against Jizan, Najran and Yanbu (energy sites) in addition to Riyadh, Jeddah and Abha. The all-but-essential-travel zone along the Yemen border now explicitly includes the cities of Abha and Khamis Mushait in Aseer province.

change_log.summary: Jordan regional-tension record updated with specific 2024/2025 border-crossing attacks
change_log.detail: FCDO advice now cites a 2025 knife attack at the King Hussein/Allenby Bridge border crossing (3 deaths) and 2024 attacks on other border crossings that killed Israeli personnel, attributed to Iran-aligned militia groups.

change_log.summary: Added Niger Delta oil & gas offshore kidnap threat to Nigeria kidnap record
change_log.detail: FCDO advice specifically flags a high threat of kidnapping and armed attacks against Niger Delta oil and gas facilities, including offshore installations — this was previously not captured in the record despite being directly relevant to oil & gas personnel.

change_log.summary: La Guaira declared a military-controlled disaster zone after June 2026 earthquakes
change_log.detail: FCDO advice now notes earthquakes on 24 June 2026 (M7.2 and M7.5) led to La Guaira state — location of Venezuela's main international airport — being declared a disaster zone under military control with strict access restrictions.

change_log.summary: Added maritime attack risk and Israeli/Jewish-linked site targeting to UAE terrorism record
change_log.detail: FCDO advice now specifically flags increased maritime attack risk for vessels in the Gulf of Oman, Northern Arabian Sea, Gulf of Aden and Bab El Mandeb, and notes Israeli and Jewish-linked sites as potential targets given regional tensions.

change_log.summary: Added 23 new countries to the dataset (4 with sourced FCDO entry/security records, 19 with basic reference facts pending full records compilation)
change_log.detail: New countries with sourced records: Bahrain, Israel, Syria, Yemen. New countries with basic reference facts only (records not yet compiled): Argentina, Congo (Republic), Côte d'Ivoire, Cameroon, Colombia, Ecuador, Gabon, Ghana, Equatorial Guinea, Guyana, Mauritania, Peru, Sudan, Senegal, Suriname, South Sudan, Chad, Tunisia, Uganda. Also added 3 new operational locations for existing oil/gas countries: East-West Pipeline Corridor (Petroline) for Saudi Arabia, and Sharara Oilfield / Zawiya for Libya.
change_log.source: Manual data merge from Claude artifact snapshot

change_log.summary: Iran border-area restricted zone expanded to Sistan/Baluchistan and area east of Bam/Jask
change_log.detail: FCDO advice against travel now also explicitly covers Sistan and Baluchistan provinces and the area east of Bam and Jask (including Bam), citing banditry and drug-trafficking risk, naming Zahedan, Zabol and Mirjaveh as particularly insecure — in addition to the existing 100km Afghanistan-border and 10km Iraq-border zones.

change_log.summary: Israel–Lebanon (Hizballah) cessation of hostilities announced 16 April 2026
change_log.detail: FCDO advice now notes a cessation of hostilities between Israel and Lebanese Hizballah was announced on 16 April 2026, though fighting continues intermittently and hostilities could reignite with little warning. Movement-restriction advice for the Lebanon border area otherwise unchanged.

change_log.summary: Houthis formally designated US and UK as hostile states following February 2026 airstrikes
change_log.detail: FCDO advice now notes that following US/UK airstrikes in February 2026, the Houthis formally designated the US and UK as hostile states, escalating the threat level for the ongoing conflict.

change_log.summary: Bahrain has temporarily banned large public gatherings on roads/squares
change_log.detail: FCDO advice now notes the Bahraini government has temporarily banned large public gatherings on roads and in squares, in addition to existing general protest-disruption guidance.

change_log.summary: Oman terrorism record broadened to include places of worship/beaches/shopping centres and a July 2024 incident
change_log.detail: FCDO advice now lists a broader set of potential terrorism targets (adding beaches, shopping centres and places of worship to the existing list) and cites a July 2024 shooting near a mosque in Muscat that killed six people.

change_log.summary: Migrated TI data structure to the event/source-observation model
change_log.detail: Added events and sourceObservations collections and schema metadata. Existing countries, records, sources, locations, change_log and oilGasSummary were preserved. Existing records retain sourceId and are grandfathered; observations are required for new records going forward.

cg.name: Congo (Republic)
cg.notes: Oil producer — deepwater Moho-Nord/Djeno fields. Distinct from the Democratic Republic of Congo. Basic reference facts only — sourced information records not yet compiled for this country.

ci.name: Côte d'Ivoire

ec.name: Ecuador
ec.notes: Amazon-basin oil producer, subject to periodic pipeline outages (spills, erosion, sabotage) on the SOTE/OCP system. Officially dollarized (uses the US Dollar). Basic reference facts only — sourced information records not yet compiled for this country.

ga.name: Gabon
ga.notes: Oil producer — Rabi-Kounga and deepwater blocks, exported via Cap Lopez. Basic reference facts only — sourced information records not yet compiled for this country.

gh.name: Ghana
gh.notes: Oil producer — Jubilee/TEN offshore fields. Basic reference facts only — sourced information records not yet compiled for this country.

gq.name: Equatorial Guinea
gq.notes: Oil & LNG producer (EG LNG, Punta Europa); 2026 reporting flags feedgas depletion risk for the single-train plant. Basic reference facts only — sourced information records not yet compiled for this country.

gy.name: Guyana
gy.notes: The fastest-growing oil producer in this dataset — Stabroek block (Liza/Payara/Yellowtail), from zero in 2019 to roughly 0.9 mb/d, with more FPSOs (Whiptail, Hammerhead) still to come. Electrical system is a mixed legacy of voltages/plug types — verify locally. Basic reference facts only — sourced information records not yet compiled for this country.

il.name: Israel
il.notes: Predominantly a gas producer (Leviathan/Tamar); crude output is marginal. Jerusalem's status as capital is internationally disputed — most foreign governments, including the UK, maintain their embassy in or near Tel Aviv. Basic reference facts only — sourced information records not yet compiled for this country.

mr.name: Mauritania
mr.notes: Crude output effectively nil (Chinguetti field depleted, ceased ~2017); current hydrocarbon story is the offshore Greater Tortue Ahmeyim (GTA) gas/LNG project shared with Senegal, not crude. Basic reference facts only — sourced information records not yet compiled for this country.

pe.name: Peru
pe.notes: Small Amazon-basin producer, frequently interrupted by pipeline spills and community blockades on the NorPeru pipeline. Basic reference facts only — sourced information records not yet compiled for this country.

sd.name: Sudan
sd.notes: Modest own crude output; larger role as transit host for South Sudan's export pipeline to Port Sudan. Ongoing internal conflict affects security conditions nationally. Basic reference facts only — sourced information records not yet compiled for this country.

sn.name: Senegal
sn.notes: New oil producer — Sangomar FPSO (first oil 2024), still ramping; also shares the offshore GTA gas project with Mauritania. Basic reference facts only — sourced information records not yet compiled for this country.

sr.name: Suriname
sr.notes: Small existing onshore output (Staatsolie); the major offshore GranMorgu (Block 58, TotalEnergies-operated) project is under construction, targeting first oil around 2028 — do not confuse today's small onshore figure with GranMorgu's eventual scale. Basic reference facts only — sourced information records not yet compiled for this country.

ss.name: South Sudan
ss.notes: Oil producer (Unity/Upper Nile fields, Nile Blend); production itself is largely intact but exports depend entirely on a pipeline through Sudan to Port Sudan that is a recurring target of drone/strike damage. Electrical standards not independently confirmed — very limited national grid. Basic reference facts only — sourced information records not yet compiled for this country.

sy.name: Syria
sy.notes: Oil producer recovering post-Assad (government fell Dec 2024); Northeast fields (Al-Omar, Deir ez-Zor basin) still consolidating from prior SDF/factional control, well below pre-war output. Ongoing security volatility nationally. Basic reference facts only — sourced information records not yet compiled for this country.

td.name: Chad
td.notes: Oil producer — Doba basin fields, exported via the Chad–Cameroon pipeline to Kribi. Basic reference facts only — sourced information records not yet compiled for this country.

tn.name: Tunisia
tn.notes: Small, mature oil producer (El Borma / Gulf of Gabes fields); exports via La Skhira. Basic reference facts only — sourced information records not yet compiled for this country.

ug.name: Uganda
ug.notes: Pre-production oil (Kingfisher/Tilenga, Lake Albert basin); the EACOP export pipeline to Tanga, Tanzania is still under construction, with first oil targeted around mid-2026 — treat any production figure as a forward target, not an actual. Basic reference facts only — sourced information records not yet compiled for this country.

ye.capital: Sana'a (constitutional; Houthi-controlled) / Aden (seat of the internationally recognised government)
ye.name: Yemen
ye.notes: Oil producer (Marib/Shabwa fields); exports resumed mid-2026 after a prolonged Houthi-related blockade but remain far below pre-war levels. Houthi forces completed capture of Yemen's Red Sea coastline and the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait 11-13 Sep 2026 (capturing Mocha and Mayyun/Perim island) — an active, evolving security situation. Electrical plug data not independently verified given the country's fragmented administration. Basic reference facts only — sourced information records not yet compiled for this country.

loc-ss-export-corridor.name: Export Pipeline Corridor (to Port Sudan)

ae-entry-medication.content: Some UK prescription and over-the-counter medicines are controlled substances in the UAE and need prior approval from the UAE Ministry of Health (max 3 months' supply, ~5 working days to process).
ae-entry-medication.title: Some UK medicines need prior approval

ae-entry-passport.content: British citizens need a passport valid at least 6 months beyond arrival for stays of 90+ days; residence permit holders and transit-only travellers need at least 3 months' validity beyond arrival/transit.
ae-entry-passport.notes: Stated for British nationals; verify equivalent rule for other nationalities.
ae-entry-passport.title: Passport validity depends on visa/stay type

ae-entry-visa.content: A visitor/tourist visa is issued free of charge on arrival, permitting up to 90 days within a rolling 180-day period, split across multiple entries if needed. Overstaying incurs daily fines.
ae-entry-visa.title: Visitor visa issued free on arrival for most stays

ae-health-medication.content: Some UK-prescribed and over-the-counter medicines are controlled substances in the UAE; prior approval from the UAE Ministry of Health is mandatory before bringing them in.
ae-health-medication.notes: Duplicates the entry-requirements note — kept here too since it's a health-relevant action item.
ae-health-medication.title: Prior approval needed for some medicines

ae-health-quality.content: Medical facilities are comparable to UK standards, but access requires travel insurance or ability to pay directly — travellers may be prevented from leaving the UAE if unable to pay a medical bill.
ae-health-quality.title: High-standard but insurance/funds essential

ae-security-driving.content: Driving standards are poor with high accident rates. Traffic violations can result in vehicle impoundment plus fines. Desert driving requires proper equipment and a companion vehicle.
ae-security-driving.title: Poor driving standards, high accident rates

ae-security-laws.content: Zero tolerance applies to drugs (even trace amounts can mean 3+ months imprisonment or large fines). Public intoxication, swearing/rude gestures, and same-sex relations are all criminal offences that have led to arrest of British nationals.
ae-security-laws.title: Strict laws carry severe penalties

ae-security-terrorism.content: The UK government assesses a high threat of terrorist attack globally affecting British interests, including in the UAE. Potential targets include residential compounds, military and oil infrastructure, transport, crowded places, hotels and shopping centres; Israeli and Jewish-linked sites are also considered potential targets given regional tensions. Vessels operating in the Gulf of Oman, Northern Arabian Sea, Gulf of Aden and Bab El Mandeb face an increased risk of maritime attack.
ae-security-terrorism.title: Terrorism risk affects the wider region including the UAE

ao-entry-currency.content: Cash or traveller's cheques valued at $5,000+ (residents $10,000+) must be declared on entry. Exit limits are $5,000 (residents $10,000) plus up to 50,000 kwanzas; airport searches may verify compliance.
ao-entry-currency.title: Cash declaration required over $5,000 ($10,000 for residents)

ao-entry-passport.content: Passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months beyond arrival and contain at least 2 blank pages. Entry is denied if the passport is invalid, expired, or reported lost/stolen.
ao-entry-passport.title: Passport valid 6 months beyond arrival, 2 blank pages

ao-entry-visa.content: No visa is needed for tourism up to 30 days. Work, study or business requires an advance visa via the Consulate General of Angola in the UK. Overstay incurs a 15,000 kwanza daily fine plus possible detention, deportation and re-entry ban.
ao-entry-visa.title: Visa-free tourism up to 30 days; visa required otherwise

ao-entry-yellowfever.content: There is a risk of yellow fever transmission in Angola. A vaccination certificate is required for onward travel to certain destinations, including South Africa.
ao-entry-yellowfever.title: Yellow fever risk present; certificate needed for onward travel

ao-health-quality.content: Private clinics in Luanda offer competent facilities but charge high fees in advance; healthcare is severely limited outside the capital. Adequate travel health insurance is essential as repatriation may be necessary.
ao-health-quality.title: Private clinics in Luanda; severely limited outside capital

ao-health-risks.content: Significant health risks include yellow fever, malaria, dengue, Zika virus, cholera, and altitude sickness in certain regions. An Ebola outbreak was declared in neighbouring DRC, which may affect border screening.
ao-health-risks.title: Yellow fever, malaria, dengue, Zika, cholera

ao-security-crime.content: High crime levels exist in Luanda, including armed muggings and fatal attacks; criminals target foreigners particularly near banks and ATMs. Theft from vehicles is common downtown; sexual assault incidents occur in nightlife areas.
ao-security-crime.title: High crime in Luanda including armed muggings

ao-security-landmines.content: Landmines and unexploded ordnance remain hazards on roads and verges outside urban centres, especially in the rainy season (November-April) when mines may shift. Travel in 4WD vehicles and avoid night driving.
ao-security-landmines.notes: Relevant for any inland oil & gas site travel outside Luanda.
ao-security-landmines.title: Landmines and unexploded ordnance on roads outside cities

ao-security-laws.content: Certified ID copies or originals must be carried outside Luanda (15,000 kwanza fine otherwise). Avoid photography near government buildings — cameras may be confiscated.
ao-security-laws.title: Carry ID outside Luanda; photography restrictions

ao-security-noall.content: The FCDO advises against all but essential travel to parts of Angola.
ao-security-noall.title: FCDO advises against all but essential travel to parts of Angola

ao-security-unrest.content: Public gatherings and demonstrations can occur with little notice and quickly turn violent — July 2025 saw three days of violent riots over fuel prices and cost of living. Monitor local media and avoid protest areas.
ao-security-unrest.title: Public gatherings can turn violent with little notice

au-emergency-ambulance.content: 000 covers ambulance, fire and police services.
au-emergency-ambulance.title: Single emergency number: 000

au-entry-biosecurity.content: Strict quarantine rules apply. Travellers must complete an Incoming Passenger Card, declare biosecurity risk items (food, animal products, plant material, wooden items), and disclose farm/animal/wilderness contact within the past 30 days. Confiscation and fines apply for violations.
au-entry-biosecurity.title: Strict biosecurity rules; declare food, animal, plant items

au-entry-passport.content: Passport must be valid for the length of planned stay; transit through other countries may require at least 6 months' remaining validity.
au-entry-passport.title: Passport valid for length of stay; 6 months for transit

au-entry-visa.content: British citizens must obtain an electronic visa: the eVisitor visa (651, free) or the Electronic Travel Authority (ETA, via app, free though service fees may apply). British-Australian dual nationals must enter/exit on their Australian passport.
au-entry-visa.title: Electronic visa required: eVisitor or ETA

au-health-quality.content: Healthcare standards are very good. The UK-Australia Reciprocal Healthcare Agreement gives UK residents access to essential and urgent medical care; hospital emergency treatment is free, though GP visits and prescriptions carry charges. Non-reciprocal visitors may face substantial costs.
au-health-quality.title: Very good; reciprocal agreement covers essential/urgent care

au-health-risks.content: Health risks include dengue, Japanese encephalitis, and other insect- or tick-borne diseases.
au-health-risks.title: Dengue, Japanese encephalitis, insect/tick-borne disease

au-security-driving.content: Vast distances between towns demand careful planning; unsurfaced roads present hazards. Carry water, GPS and spare tyres, and inform others of travel plans on remote routes.
au-security-driving.title: Vast distances; unsurfaced remote roads

au-security-naturaldisaster.content: Bushfire risk exists year-round, peaking November-February. Tropical cyclones affect Queensland, NT and WA November-April. Flooding follows heavy rainfall and cyclones; follow 'stay-at-home' or 'leave-now' orders immediately. Extreme heatwaves pose health risks throughout the continent.
au-security-naturaldisaster.title: Bushfires, cyclones and flooding by season/region

au-security-terrorism.content: There is a high threat of terrorist attack globally affecting UK interests and British nationals, and terrorists are likely to attempt attacks in Australia. Recent incidents include a December 2025 antisemitic attack at Bondi Beach (15 deaths) and an April 2024 church incident in Wakeley, Sydney.
au-security-terrorism.title: High global threat; recent attacks in Sydney/Bondi

au-security-wildlife.content: Dangerous wildlife includes crocodiles, venomous snakes and spiders, sharks and jellyfish. Rip currents threaten swimmers.
au-security-wildlife.title: Crocodiles, snakes, sharks and jellyfish

az-entry-passport.content: Visitors need a passport valid for at least 6 months after arrival with 2 blank pages for stamps. Residents need at least 3 months' validity beyond their residence permit expiry.
az-entry-passport.title: Passport valid 6 months beyond arrival, 2 blank pages

az-entry-registration.content: Stays exceeding 15 days require online or in-person registration with the State Migration Service; failure incurs exit fines.
az-entry-registration.title: Stays over 15 days require registration

az-entry-visa.content: A visa is mandatory for all visits. Apply via the ASAN Visa e-visa service at least 3 days in advance; single-entry visas allow 30-day stays within a 90-day validity period. Business/work visas require contacting the Azerbaijani Embassy at least one month before travel.
az-entry-visa.title: E-visa mandatory; apply via ASAN Visa at least 3 days ahead

az-health-quality.content: Medical facilities outside Baku are very limited. Even in the capital, serious illness or injury may require evacuation to Turkey or Western Europe. Carry a first aid kit for trips outside Baku.
az-health-quality.notes: Relevant for any Caspian/offshore oil & gas site travel outside Baku.
az-health-quality.title: Very limited outside Baku; evacuation may be needed

az-health-risks.content: Altitude sickness is a risk in mountain areas including the Shahdag and Tufangdag ski resorts, Lake Batabat in Nakhchivan, and the Talysh mountains.
az-health-risks.title: Altitude sickness in mountain resort areas

az-security-borderzone.content: The FCDO advises against all travel within 5km of the Armenia border due to landmine and unexploded ordnance risk from the 2020 and 2023 conflicts. Southwest regions affected by conflict carry similar risks.
az-security-borderzone.title: No travel within 5km of the Armenia border

az-security-crime.content: Baku has generally low crime, though bag-snatching and mugging occur, particularly after dark. Guard against card skimming at ATMs and during transactions.
az-security-crime.title: Generally low crime in Baku; bag-snatching after dark

az-security-laws.content: Illegal drugs (including cannabis) carry severe jail sentences and heavy fines. Drones are prohibited for non-residents without a special permit. Photography of military installations risks detention.
az-security-laws.title: Drugs carry severe penalties; drone/photography restrictions

az-security-terrorism.content: Terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Azerbaijan, with potential targets including hotels, restaurants, energy sector facilities, religious sites, shopping centres, embassies and transport hubs.
az-security-terrorism.notes: Fast-changing — review at least quarterly. Energy sector explicitly named as a target category — directly relevant to oil & gas travel.
az-security-terrorism.title: Energy sector facilities identified as potential targets

br-emergency-ambulance.content: Call 192 and ask for an ambulance.
br-emergency-ambulance.title: Ambulance emergency number: 192

br-entry-passport.content: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your arrival date. Make sure the border control officer stamps your passport — if it isn't stamped, you may be fined on departure.
br-entry-passport.title: Passport valid 6+ months; ensure entry stamp is applied

br-entry-visa.content: British citizens can visit visa-free for up to 90 days for tourism. To extend, contact the Federal Police before the visa expires; overstaying incurs daily fines payable on departure or a later visit.
br-entry-visa.title: Visa-free for up to 90 days for tourism

br-health-diseases.content: Brazil poses disease risks including yellow fever, dengue, chikungunya and oropouche, alongside high UV exposure and altitude sickness in some regions.
br-health-diseases.title: Yellow fever, dengue, chikungunya and oropouche risk

br-health-hospitals.content: Public hospitals in major cities are overcrowded with long waits and medication shortages, though foreign nationals do receive emergency treatment. Private hospitals require proof of financial capacity or insurance before admission.
br-health-hospitals.title: Public hospitals overcrowded; private needs proof of funds/insurance

br-security-crime.content: Robberies are common in many cities, particularly on buses, with mobile phones frequently targeted 4pm-9pm. Beach theft includes organised group robberies ('arrastões'). Express kidnapping — short abductions to force ATM withdrawals — also occurs.
br-security-crime.title: Robbery, pickpocketing and express kidnapping in cities

br-security-essential.content: The FCDO advises against all but essential travel to certain parts of Brazil — check the specific areas before travelling.
br-security-essential.title: FCDO advises against all but essential travel to parts of Brazil

br-security-favelas.content: Favelas (informal urban neighbourhoods) pose unpredictable danger; tourists have been shot after accidentally entering favelas. Avoid favela tours and accommodation, and check that GPS navigation doesn't route through them.
br-security-favelas.title: Avoid favelas — unpredictable danger, including to tourists

ca-emergency-ambulance.content: Dial 911 and ask for an ambulance.
ca-emergency-ambulance.title: Emergency number: 911

ca-entry-eta.content: Most short visits (typically up to 6 months) need an Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) rather than a visa; this isn't required if arriving by land/sea with acceptable ID, or for dual British-Canadian nationals travelling on a valid Canadian passport.
ca-entry-eta.title: eTA usually required instead of a visa for short visits

ca-entry-passport.content: Your passport must be valid for the duration of your stay in Canada; many transit countries separately require at least 6 months' remaining validity.
ca-entry-passport.title: Passport valid for duration of stay; 6 months for onward transit

ca-health-cost.content: Medical treatment can be very expensive with no special arrangements for British visitors; access emergency care via hospital emergency rooms or walk-in clinics.
ca-health-cost.title: Medical treatment can be very expensive for visitors

ca-security-cannabis.content: Cannabis is legal for recreational use within Canada, but it is illegal to take cannabis across the Canadian border without a permit or exemption — severe penalties apply.
ca-security-cannabis.title: Cannabis legal in Canada but illegal to cross the border with it

ca-security-terrorism.content: There is a significant threat of terrorist attacks in Canada, which could be indiscriminate and affect places visited by foreign nationals.
ca-security-terrorism.title: Significant threat of terrorist attack

ca-security-wildfire.content: Western Canada faces a significant wildfire risk in summer — follow local warnings and news for the latest outbreaks. Winter storms (November-April) bring blizzards and freezing rain causing dangerous driving conditions.
ca-security-wildfire.title: Wildfires common in western Canada in summer

cn-emergency-ambulance.content: Call 120 and ask for an ambulance.
cn-emergency-ambulance.title: Ambulance emergency number: 120

cn-entry-passport.content: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your arrival date and have 2 blank pages for visas and stamps.
cn-entry-passport.title: Passport valid 6+ months, 2 blank pages

cn-entry-registration.content: Register your residence with local police authorities within 24 hours of arrival, and expect biometric data (fingerprints, photos) to be collected on entry.
cn-entry-registration.title: Register residence with local authorities within 24 hours

cn-entry-visafree.content: Until 31 December 2026, British citizens can enter China visa-free for stays up to 30 days for business, tourism, or family/friend visits. Longer stays, work, or study require a visa arranged in advance — a tourist/business visa does not permit working.
cn-entry-visafree.notes: Time-limited exemption — re-verify closer to end of 2026.
cn-entry-visafree.title: Visa-free for up to 30 days until 31 Dec 2026

cn-health-cost.content: Medical care in China is not subsidised for visitors and carries substantial costs. Comprehensive travel insurance covering healthcare, evacuation and repatriation is essential.
cn-health-cost.title: Medical care not subsidised for visitors — comprehensive insurance essential

cn-health-water.content: Tap water is unsafe in China; consume only bottled water. Notable disease risks include avian influenza and dengue fever (concentrated in Guangdong Province, mainly May-November).
cn-health-water.title: Tap water is unsafe — drink bottled water only

cn-security-detention.content: China's broad national security laws mean foreigners may be detained without having intended to break the law, potentially for up to 6 months before formal charges. Exit bans can be imposed for commercial disputes or investigations, lasting months or years without notice.
cn-security-detention.title: Broad security laws create arbitrary detention risk

cn-security-drugs.content: Drug possession carries severe penalties including lengthy imprisonment or the death penalty; random drug testing occurs at borders and in public spaces.
cn-security-drugs.title: Severe penalties for drug offences, including death penalty

cn-security-terrorism.content: Terrorist attacks in China cannot be ruled out, particularly in places frequented by foreigners during national holidays and at transport hubs.
cn-security-terrorism.title: Attacks cannot be ruled out, especially around holidays

dz-entry-currency.content: Cash exceeding €5,000 or equivalent must be declared at entry/exit; failure to declare is a criminal offence. Only residents may bring in Algerian dinars (max 10,000).
dz-entry-currency.title: Cash over €5,000 must be declared

dz-entry-passport.content: Passport must remain valid for at least 6 months beyond the arrival date. Invalid, lost or stolen documents will result in denial of entry.
dz-entry-passport.title: Passport valid 6 months beyond arrival

dz-entry-visa.content: A visa is mandatory for all visitors, obtained before travel via the Algerian Consulate in the UK (tourist visas may be available on arrival at certain southern airports with an approved local travel agency reservation). Overstaying risks detention, prosecution and up to 3 months' imprisonment.
dz-entry-visa.title: Visa mandatory for all visitors; overstay risks prison

dz-health-quality.content: Private clinics offer better facilities than government hospitals; English is not widely spoken. Adequate travel health insurance and accessible funds for medical costs and repatriation are recommended.
dz-health-quality.title: Private clinics better than government hospitals

dz-health-risks.content: Altitude sickness is a notable risk in certain regions; consult TravelHealthPro for a full risk assessment.
dz-health-risks.title: Altitude sickness in certain regions

dz-security-driving.content: Algeria has a very high road traffic accident rate with erratic driving and minimal lane discipline; hazards include sand drifts, potholes and speed bumps.
dz-security-driving.title: Very high accident rate; sand drifts and potholes

dz-security-kidnap.content: A significant kidnap threat exists from groups such as AQIM and Daesh-affiliated organisations operating across North Africa; British nationals are considered legitimate targets. The UK government does not pay ransoms.
dz-security-kidnap.title: Significant kidnap threat from AQIM and Daesh-affiliated groups

dz-security-laws.content: Zero tolerance applies to drugs (penalties can include the death penalty). Public intoxication is illegal. Sexual acts between same-sex partners are illegal. Ramadan restrictions apply on eating, drinking and smoking in public.
dz-security-laws.title: Zero tolerance for drugs; same-sex relations illegal

dz-security-noall.content: The FCDO advises against all travel to parts of Algeria, particularly the southern border regions (kidnap concentration area), the Libyan and Tunisian borders, rural/mountainous areas north of Algiers, and the Sahara region.
dz-security-noall.notes: Fast-changing — review at least monthly. Relevant to any Sahara/desert oil & gas operations.
dz-security-noall.title: FCDO advises against all travel to southern border/Sahara areas

dz-security-terrorism.content: Terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Algeria; attacks may target foreign nationals, including via lone actors. Recent incidents include IED attacks on soldiers in 2021.
dz-security-terrorism.title: High terrorism threat; attacks likely

eg-entry-currency.content: Maximum 5,000 Egyptian pounds in/out; foreign currency over 10,000 USD must be declared. High-value electronics and recording equipment must be declared. Satellite phones/radio equipment are subject to confiscation without Ministry clearance.
eg-entry-currency.notes: Satellite phone rule is operationally relevant for remote oil & gas site communications equipment.
eg-entry-currency.title: Currency declaration rules; equipment restrictions

eg-entry-passport.content: Passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after arrival and at least one blank page.
eg-entry-passport.title: Passport valid 6 months beyond arrival, one blank page

eg-entry-visa.content: British passport holders typically need a visa: online e-visa (valid up to 3 months), via the Egyptian Consulate, or on arrival at approved airports (30 USD cash, valid up to 30 days). No visa is required for under-15-day stays in Sharm El-Sheikh, Dahab, Nuweiba or Taba resorts if arriving by air. Digital visas at Cairo Airport from 1 Aug 2026 cost 36 USD by card.
eg-entry-visa.title: Visa required; e-visa, on-arrival, or Sharm exemption available

eg-health-medication.content: Certain prescription and over-the-counter medications are controlled substances in Egypt and may require prior authorisation from Egypt's Ministry of Health. Travellers should carry a GP letter documenting condition, dosage and personal use, or risk confiscation and prosecution.
eg-health-medication.title: Some medicines controlled; prior authorisation may be needed

eg-health-quality.content: Some hotel doctors have significantly overcharged patients, though pharmacies outside hotels are more affordable. Specialised psychiatric care is limited outside major cities.
eg-health-quality.title: Hotel doctors may overcharge; specialist care limited

eg-health-risks.content: Health risks include dengue fever and tick-borne illnesses, particularly Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever; altitude sickness is a risk in certain regions.
eg-health-risks.title: Dengue and tick-borne illness including CCHF

eg-security-crime.content: Overall crime rates are low, but sexual assaults have been reported, particularly at Red Sea resorts, often involving accommodation staff. Female travellers should avoid solo taxi rides, especially at night.
eg-security-crime.title: Low overall crime; sexual assault reports at Red Sea resorts

eg-security-laws.content: Foreign nationals risk detention for political activity or government criticism, including social media posts. Drug possession carries life imprisonment or the death penalty. Photography requires permits near military/government sites; drones are prohibited without Ministry of Defence approval.
eg-security-laws.title: Political criticism risky; drug possession severe

eg-security-noall.content: The FCDO advises against all travel to certain regions and against all but essential travel to other parts — see the regional risks page for Sinai-specific detail.
eg-security-noall.title: FCDO advises against travel to parts of Sinai

eg-security-terrorism.content: Terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Egypt, potentially targeting security forces, religious sites, public gatherings and foreign nationals. Recent incidents include a 2024 shooting in Alexandria and 2023 attacks on Israeli tourists.
eg-security-terrorism.title: Attacks likely; may target security forces and foreign nationals

es-entry-ees.content: The EU's Entry/Exit System requires biometric registration (fingerprints and photo) on first entry to the Schengen area; free of charge and valid for three years.
es-entry-ees.title: EU Entry/Exit System (EES) biometric registration

es-entry-passport.content: Your passport must have been issued less than 10 years before your arrival date, and have an expiry date at least 3 months after you plan to leave the Schengen area. Passports renewed before 1 October 2018 may be affected.
es-entry-passport.notes: Stated for British nationals; verify equivalent rule for other nationalities.
es-entry-passport.title: Passport must meet Schengen age/validity rules

es-entry-visa.content: British citizens can enter visa-free for tourism, family visits, events or short study for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Time spent in other Schengen countries counts towards this limit; overstaying risks a 3-year Schengen ban.
es-entry-visa.title: Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period

es-health-quality.content: Public healthcare is generally adequate, but tourist areas may lack nearby public facilities, and private doctors/hospitals do not accept GHIC/EHIC cards. Travel insurance remains essential for repatriation and non-urgent treatment.
es-health-quality.title: GHIC/EHIC does not replace travel insurance

es-security-balearics.content: Specific resort areas (Magaluf, Playa de Palma, San Antonio in Ibiza) see recurring dangerous balcony incidents and illegal commercial parties.
es-security-balearics.title: Balcony falls and illegal parties in resort areas

es-security-terrorism.content: The UK assesses a high threat of terrorist attack globally, and terrorists are considered likely to try to carry out attacks in Spain. Attacks can be indiscriminate, including in places visited by foreigners.
es-security-terrorism.title: Terrorism threat assessed as high

es-security-theft.content: Organised theft using distraction tactics is common, particularly at airports and around luggage handling. 'Highway pirates' target foreign-registered and hire vehicles; scammers may pose as plainclothes police to rob travellers.
es-security-theft.title: Organised theft targets tourists, especially at airports

gb-emergency-ambulance.content: 999 (or the EU-standard 112) covers ambulance, fire and police services nationally.
gb-emergency-ambulance.title: Emergency number: 999 (or 112)

gb-entry-eta.content: Most visitors to the UK need an ETA (Electronic Travel Authorisation) or a visa; requirement depends on nationality and purpose of visit. British and Irish passport holders, and those with permission to live/work/study in the UK, do not need an ETA. An ETA costs £20, is applied for online, and permits travel to the UK, Jersey, Guernsey or the Isle of Man for up to 6 months.
gb-entry-eta.notes: Nationality-dependent — check gov.uk for the specific traveller's passport before booking.
gb-entry-eta.title: Most visitors need an ETA or visa depending on nationality

gb-entry-passport.content: A passport or travel document is required to enter the UK and should be valid for the whole of the stay (no fixed minimum extra-validity period is stated, unlike many other countries).
gb-entry-passport.title: Passport must be valid for the whole stay

gb-entry-visitorvisa.content: Nationalities that need a visa (rather than an ETA) can apply for a Standard Visitor visa, allowing tourism, family visits, business meetings and permitted paid engagements for up to 6 months. It costs £135 and can be applied for up to 3 months before travel. Paid or unpaid work (other than permitted engagements) is prohibited on this route.
gb-entry-visitorvisa.notes: Relevant for non-ETA-eligible personnel (e.g. some Middle East/Africa passport holders) visiting UK offices.
gb-entry-visitorvisa.title: Standard Visitor visa allows up to 6 months for business/tourism

gb-health-nhs.content: Healthcare in the UK is of a high standard via the National Health Service (NHS). Emergency treatment is provided regardless of nationality, but visitors from countries without a reciprocal healthcare agreement with the UK may be charged for treatment, including hospital care.
gb-health-nhs.title: NHS treatment; visitors from non-reciprocal countries may be charged

gb-security-general.content: The UK is not covered by FCDO self-facing travel advice since it is the issuing government; general safety levels are consistent with a developed Western European country. Ordinary situational-awareness precautions (as in any major city) are sufficient for routine business travel.
gb-security-general.notes: No official FCDO 'advice against travel' equivalent exists for the UK — this is Claude's contextual summary, not a sourced FCDO record like other countries.
gb-security-general.title: Low routine risk; standard UK safety precautions apply

id-entry-declaration.content: Complete the 'All Indonesia Declaration Form' online within 72 hours of arrival (free). Register with local police if staying in private accommodation (5 million rupiah fine otherwise). A Bali tourist levy of 150,000 rupiah applies on arrival in Bali.
id-entry-declaration.title: Online arrival declaration and Bali tourist levy

id-entry-passport.content: Passport must be valid for at least 6 months after arrival and have at least 2 blank pages.
id-entry-passport.title: Passport valid 6 months beyond arrival, 2 blank pages

id-entry-visa.content: A visa is mandatory. Visa-on-arrival (500,000 IDR, 30 days, single entry) is available at major airports/seaports for tourism and some business; online visas can be applied for at least a week ahead with multiple-entry/60-day options, but must be approved before arrival. The 30-day visa can be extended once for a further 30 days within the initial period.
id-entry-visa.title: Visa mandatory; visa-on-arrival (30 days) or online e-visa options

id-health-quality.content: Standards of local medical care can be poor and some tests cannot be performed reliably; psychological services are particularly limited. Remote areas lack capacity for serious injury/illness; good care can be prohibitively expensive.
id-health-quality.title: Inconsistent standards; remote areas lack serious-injury capacity

id-health-risks.content: Health risks include unhealthy air quality during dry-season wildfires (May-November), volcanic ash exposure, Zika virus, dengue fever, malaria, and rabies from street dogs and monkeys.
id-health-risks.title: Air quality, Zika, dengue, malaria, rabies

id-health-water.content: Tap water is not safe to drink in Indonesia.
id-health-water.title: Tap water is not safe to drink

id-security-crime.content: High rates of sexual assault are reported in Bali and Lombok; avoid poorly lit areas at night. Drink spiking incidents are documented in Bali, Lombok and the Gili Islands. Counterfeit alcohol containing methanol has caused deaths.
id-security-crime.title: Sexual assault and drink-spiking reported in Bali/Lombok

id-security-laws.content: All forms of cannabis are illegal with airports using advanced detection technology; drug possession carries lengthy prison sentences or the death penalty. Aceh Province enforces Sharia law, banning alcohol and prohibiting LGBT+ activity, gambling and extramarital relations.
id-security-laws.title: Zero tolerance for drugs; Sharia law in Aceh

id-security-naturaldisaster.content: Volcanoes are active throughout Indonesia and can erupt without warning, with evacuation zones typically 3-7km. Earthquakes and tsunamis occur regularly. Flooding is common October-March; wildfires April-September generate widespread haze.
id-security-naturaldisaster.title: Active volcanoes, earthquakes and tsunamis

id-security-noall.content: The FCDO advises against all travel to parts of Indonesia — see the regional risks guidance for specific areas.
id-security-noall.title: FCDO advises against all travel to parts of Indonesia

id-security-terrorism.content: Terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Indonesia. Islamist extremism remains elevated, with potential targets including beach resorts, hotels, markets, tourist attractions, embassies and airports. Heightened risk periods include Christmas, New Year, Easter, Chinese New Year, Ramadan and elections.
id-security-terrorism.title: High threat; targets include resorts, hotels and airports

iq-entry-bloodtest.content: Unless on a visit visa, travellers must undergo HIV and hepatitis testing within 10 days of arrival, repeated every 90 days.
iq-entry-bloodtest.title: HIV/hepatitis testing required for longer stays

iq-entry-currency.content: Declare local currency exceeding 200,000 Iraqi dinars, or foreign currency/valuables over $10,000 USD equivalent.
iq-entry-currency.title: Currency declaration thresholds

iq-entry-evisa.content: A visa is mandatory for all visits, applied for via the Government of Iraq e-visa portal at least 24 hours before travel ($160 USD, valid for a 60-day stay). A return or onward ticket is normally required. The Kurdistan Region has a separate e-visa/visa-on-arrival scheme valid only within that region.
iq-entry-evisa.title: E-visa required via Iraqi government portal (60-day stay)

iq-entry-passport.content: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your arrival date and contain at least one blank page. Passports reported lost or stolen will result in entry denial.
iq-entry-passport.title: Passport must be valid 6+ months, one blank page

iq-health-risks.content: Iraq presents health risks including Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever and malaria, plus respiratory risk from dust/sand storms and altitude sickness in some regions.
iq-health-risks.title: Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever and malaria present

iq-security-civilunrest.content: Regular protests occur, sometimes with casualties. Curfews and vehicle bans may be imposed suddenly around holidays, pilgrimages or elections. Anti-British/American sentiment can escalate during political tensions.
iq-security-civilunrest.title: Protests, curfews and vehicle bans can occur with little warning

iq-security-kidnap.content: There is a high threat of kidnapping throughout Iraq from terrorist and militant groups including Daesh. British nationals — including oil workers, business travellers and humanitarian workers — are considered legitimate targets. The UK government does not pay ransoms.
iq-security-kidnap.title: High threat of kidnapping nationwide

iq-security-terrorism.content: Terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Iraq, particularly in provinces with former Daesh strongholds (Anbar, Diyala, Ninewah, Salah Al-Din, Kirkuk). Attacks include bombings, rockets, mortars, shootings and vehicle-borne explosives, targeting airports, markets, hotels, government buildings and religious sites. Foreign nationals, including oil workers, are considered high-value targets.
iq-security-terrorism.title: Very high threat of terrorist attack nationwide

ir-entry-visa.content: A visa is mandatory (unless holding an Iranian passport), obtained either through an organised tour or with an in-country sponsor; the process is described as long and unpredictable, so apply well in advance. Passports with Israeli stamps may be denied entry, and Iran does not recognise dual nationality.
ir-entry-visa.notes: The FCDO advises against all travel — see the SECURITY category.
ir-entry-visa.title: Visa required via organised tour or in-country sponsor

ir-health-quality.content: Medical infrastructure varies considerably by location — urban centres offer reasonable facilities but remote areas have limited services, and there have been documented shortages of basic medicines nationwide.
ir-health-quality.title: Variable quality; shortages of basic medicines reported

ir-security-advisory.content: The FCDO advises against all travel to Iran and warns British nationals face risk of arrest, detention and even a death sentence. The UK cannot guarantee evacuation or face-to-face consular assistance during a crisis.
ir-security-advisory.notes: Fast-changing — review at least monthly. Directly relevant given regional oil & gas work.
ir-security-advisory.title: FCDO advises against all travel to Iran

ir-security-borderareas.content: Travel within 100km of the Afghanistan border, within 10km of the Iraq border, to Sistan and Baluchistan provinces, or to the area east of Bam and Jask (including Bam) is strongly advised against, due to banditry and drug-trafficking risk — Zahedan, Zabol and Mirjaveh are considered particularly insecure.
ir-security-borderareas.title: Avoid travel near the Afghanistan and Iraq borders

ir-security-detention.content: Holding a British passport or perceived UK connections can be reason enough for detention. British-Iranian dual nationals may not be notified to the UK government if detained, and consular access is not guaranteed. Risk increases for anyone linked to civil society, journalism, or with connections to Israel or the US.
ir-security-detention.title: Very high risk of arrest/detention, especially for dual nationals

jo-entry-passport.content: Your passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after the date you arrive in Jordan.
jo-entry-passport.notes: Stated for British nationals; verify equivalent rule for other nationalities.
jo-entry-passport.title: Passport must be valid at least 6 months beyond arrival

jo-entry-registration.content: Visitors remaining over 14 days must register with local police within that timeframe, providing biometrics. Failure results in a 200 JOD fine on departure.
jo-entry-registration.title: Stays over 14 days require police registration

jo-entry-visa.content: A visa is mandatory. Options include a single-entry visa on arrival at airports/the Sheikh Hussein or North Border crossing (40 JOD, 3 months validity), or the Jordan Pass for tourism stays of 3+ nights (70-80 JOD, applied for online before arrival, includes tourist-site discounts). Non-tourism visits should apply in advance via the Ministry of Interior.
jo-entry-visa.title: Visa on arrival, or Jordan Pass for tourism stays of 3+ nights

jo-health-facilities.content: Medical facilities outside Amman and Aqaba are basic; in an emergency, seek treatment in Amman or Aqaba.
jo-health-facilities.title: Medical facilities outside Amman and Aqaba are basic

jo-security-regionaltension.content: There is a risk of escalating regional conflict. Iran-aligned militia groups have threatened to target US interests across the region and have claimed attacks in Jordan, including a 2025 knife attack at the King Hussein/Allenby Bridge border crossing (3 deaths) and 2024 attacks on other border crossings that killed Israeli personnel. Avoid military/strategic facilities, follow local advice to shelter if instructed, and expect possible flight cancellations and airspace closures.
jo-security-regionaltension.title: Risk of regional escalation, including strikes near Aqaba

jo-security-syriaborder.content: The FCDO advises against all travel within 3km of the border with Syria.
jo-security-syriaborder.title: Avoid all travel within 3km of the Syria border

jp-entry-passport.content: Your passport must remain valid for the whole of your stay and have a blank page for the visa stamp. Passports reported lost or stolen will result in entry denial.
jp-entry-passport.title: Passport must be valid for duration of stay, one blank page

jp-entry-visa.content: British citizens can get a visa on arrival for tourism or business for up to 90 days without prior application; a further 90-day extension can be requested at a local immigration office. Work or study requires an appropriate visa arranged beforehand — overstaying can mean arrest, detention and a heavy fine.
jp-entry-visa.title: Visa on arrival for tourism/business up to 90 days

jp-health-cost.content: Medical facilities are high standard, but treatment is expensive with patients responsible for full costs and insurance checks that may delay treatment.
jp-health-cost.title: High standard but expensive; full cost due upfront

jp-health-medication.content: Japan enforces strict anti-stimulant drug laws; some common items such as Vicks inhalers and certain allergy/cold medications or painkillers are banned. Foreign nationals have been detained and deported for bringing them in — verify medication legality with the Japanese Embassy in the UK beforehand.
jp-health-medication.title: Strict bans on common medicines (e.g. some inhalers, allergy/cold medicine)

jp-security-druggedcrime.content: Tokyo's entertainment districts (Kabukicho, Roppongi, Shibuya, Ikebukuro) carry a higher risk of crime at night. Victims of drink-spiking scams have reported large unauthorised credit card charges. Avoid touts who approach speaking English.
jp-security-druggedcrime.title: Drink-spiking and fraud in Tokyo entertainment districts

jp-security-earthquake.content: Japan is in a major earthquake zone with associated tsunami risk. Monitor local alerts and follow local authority instructions. Typhoon season runs June-December (peak July-September), bringing high tides, landslide and flood risk. Multiple active volcanoes require monitoring of local alerts.
jp-security-earthquake.title: Japan is in a major earthquake and tsunami zone

jp-security-legal.content: Travellers can be detained without charge for up to 23 days for minor offences. Drug possession carries zero tolerance with sentences of 6-17 years. You must carry your passport or residence card at all times.
jp-security-legal.title: Detention without charge possible; zero tolerance on drugs

kw-emergency-ambulance.content: Call 112 and ask for an ambulance.
kw-emergency-ambulance.title: Ambulance emergency number: 112

kw-entry-israelstamp.content: If your passport contains an Israeli stamp, you may be denied entry or a visa.
kw-entry-israelstamp.title: Israeli passport stamps may cause entry/visa refusal

kw-entry-passport.content: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your arrival date; for residency visas, at least 2 years' validity is required.
kw-entry-passport.title: Passport valid 6+ months (2 years for residency visas)

kw-entry-visa.content: A visa is mandatory, available on arrival at Kuwaiti airports or online via the Ministry of Interior. British citizens born in Afghanistan, Iran, Iraq, Lebanon, Pakistan, Sudan, Syria or Yemen cannot get a visa on arrival and must apply through the Kuwaiti Embassy beforehand.
kw-entry-visa.notes: Relevant given oil & gas travellers' varied birthplaces/travel histories.
kw-entry-visa.title: Visa on arrival or online — exceptions for some birthplaces

kw-health-medication.content: Under Kuwaiti rules, visitors must obtain permission from the Kuwaiti authorities to carry certain prescription drugs before arrival — this covers many commonly prescribed medications, so prepare documentation well in advance.
kw-health-medication.title: Prior permission needed for certain prescription drugs

kw-security-borders.content: It is illegal and dangerous to go near Kuwait's borders with Iraq and Saudi Arabia without authorisation; armed patrols are routine and unexploded landmines remain present in some areas — avoid off-road driving.
kw-security-borders.title: Illegal and dangerous to approach Kuwait's borders without authorisation

kw-security-terrorism.content: There is a high threat of terrorist attack globally affecting British interests. Iran-aligned militia groups have threatened US interests regionally and conducted missile/drone attacks; potential targets include residential compounds, hotels, shopping centres and oil/transport infrastructure.
kw-security-terrorism.title: High global terrorism threat; Iran-aligned militia activity in the region

kz-emergency-ambulance.content: Ambulance emergency number: 103 (operators may not speak English).
kz-emergency-ambulance.title: Ambulance emergency number: 103

kz-entry-currency.content: Cash declarations are required for amounts exceeding $10,000 USD on arrival; undeclared amounts may be confiscated with fines. Export is limited to $10,000 USD in foreign currency cash.
kz-entry-currency.title: Cash declaration required over $10,000

kz-entry-passport.content: Passport must be valid for at least 30 days from arrival with one blank page minimum. If holding a Kazakh visa, passport must expire at least 3 months after the visa's expiry.
kz-entry-passport.title: Passport valid 30 days from arrival, one blank page

kz-entry-registration.content: Accommodation providers or hosts must register a traveller's arrival with the authorities within 3 working days of entry.
kz-entry-registration.title: Accommodation must register arrival within 3 working days

kz-entry-visa.content: Visa-free entry for up to 30 days for business or tourism, with unlimited visits allowed, but cannot exceed 90 days without a visa in any rolling 180-day period. Longer stays, work or study require a visa/work permit.
kz-entry-visa.title: Visa-free up to 30 days; max 90 days per 180-day period

kz-health-quality.content: Medical facilities are less advanced than UK standards and most staff do not speak English. Adequate travel health insurance and accessible funds for treatment or evacuation are essential.
kz-health-quality.title: Facilities less advanced than UK; insurance essential

kz-health-risks.content: Health risks include biting insects and ticks, and altitude sickness in mountainous regions.
kz-health-risks.title: Biting insects/ticks and altitude sickness

kz-security-crime.content: Robberies and violent theft occur mainly at night in expatriate areas (Atyrau, Aktau, Astana, Almaty) near nightclubs and bars. Pickpocketing is common in markets and on public transport. Drink spiking leading to assault has been reported.
kz-security-crime.notes: Atyrau and Aktau are the main Caspian oil-industry hub cities — directly relevant for oil & gas travel.
kz-security-crime.title: Robbery, pickpocketing and drink-spiking risk in cities

kz-security-laws.content: It is illegal to sell, distribute, import or produce e-cigarettes, vapes or e-liquid (up to 2 years' imprisonment). Disrespectful social media posts about religion, culture or national symbols are illegal. Drones require a licence. LGBT+ 'promotion' legislation introduced December 2025 risks fines, detention or deportation.
kz-security-laws.title: Vaping/e-cigarettes illegal; strict speech and LGBT+ laws

kz-security-restricted-areas.content: Gvardeyskiy village (Almaty region), Baikonur town, and Karmakchi and Kazalinsk districts (Kyzylorda region) are restricted without special permission.
kz-security-restricted-areas.title: Some areas require special permission

kz-security-terrorism.content: Terrorist attacks in Kazakhstan cannot be ruled out and could be indiscriminate, including in places visited by foreign nationals.
kz-security-terrorism.title: Terrorist attacks cannot be ruled out

ly-emergency-ambulance.content: Ambulance emergency number: 1415. Medical help in remote areas may not be available and rescue operations have uncertain status.
ly-emergency-ambulance.title: Ambulance emergency number: 1415

ly-entry-cash.content: Libya is a cash-based society — bank cards cannot be used at banks, ATMs or hotels, and ATM access is severely restricted. Amounts over $10,000 USD must be declared. Exporting Libyan dinar is illegal; use only Central Bank-approved exchange offices.
ly-entry-cash.notes: Operationally significant for any personnel travelling to Libya — arrange cash logistics before travel.
ly-entry-cash.title: Cash-based society; bank cards largely unusable

ly-entry-passport.content: Passport must be valid for the entire duration of stay. Passports showing previous travel to Israel will be rejected. Lost or stolen passports result in entry denial.
ly-entry-passport.title: Passport valid for full stay; Israel stamps rejected

ly-entry-registration.content: All short-stay visitors must register with police within one week of arrival; failure results in fines on departure. This is typically handled by the host company or travel agency.
ly-entry-registration.title: Police registration required within one week

ly-entry-visa.content: A visa is mandatory, obtained via the Libyan Embassy in London. A Libyan visa issued overseas may not be recognised in some areas or at certain ports of entry due to the current political situation.
ly-entry-visa.notes: Fast-changing given the fragmented political/security situation — review at least quarterly.
ly-entry-visa.title: Visa mandatory; overseas-issued visas may not be recognised everywhere

ly-health-quality.content: Healthcare is substandard compared to UK facilities, with acute shortages of skilled personnel and medical supplies, particularly for chronic conditions such as diabetes. Private clinics exist in Tripoli, but medical evacuation to Malta or Europe may be necessary for serious conditions.
ly-health-quality.title: Substandard; evacuation to Malta/Europe often needed

ly-health-risks.content: Key health risks include leishmaniasis, West Nile virus, and schistosomiasis.
ly-health-risks.title: Leishmaniasis, West Nile virus, schistosomiasis

ly-security-areas.content: Avoid border regions with Mali, Niger and Algeria (extremist group activity) and the coastal road between Zawiyah and Tripoli (very high carjacking/robbery risk). Southern Fezzan Province has the highest terrorist concentration.
ly-security-areas.title: Avoid border regions and the Zawiyah-Tripoli coastal road

ly-security-conflict.content: The political situation is fragile and the security situation remains dangerous and unpredictable. A UN-facilitated ceasefire exists between eastern and western forces, though localised armed group violence persists — armed clashes broke out in Tripoli in May 2024 and August 2023.
ly-security-conflict.title: Fragile political situation; localised armed clashes persist

ly-security-kidnap.content: Terrorist groups in Libya have intent to carry out kidnappings targeting foreign nationals; criminal gangs also kidnap and may sell hostages to terrorist groups. Oil and gas workers are highly likely to be viewed as high-value targets, and British nationals are considered high-value hostages.
ly-security-kidnap.notes: Fast-changing — review at least monthly. Directly relevant to any oil & gas personnel travel to Libya.
ly-security-kidnap.title: Oil and gas workers viewed as high-value targets

ly-security-noall.content: The FCDO advises against all travel to parts of Libya and against all but essential travel to other parts.
ly-security-noall.title: FCDO advises against all/all but essential travel to parts of Libya

ly-security-terrorism.content: Terrorist attacks in Libya cannot be ruled out and may target locations frequented by foreigners. Daesh and AQIM operate primarily in the Fezzan Province (south) but can move to other areas. Recent attacks include a 2022 car bombing near a military camp.
ly-security-terrorism.title: High terrorism threat; Daesh/AQIM active in Fezzan

mx-emergency-ambulance.content: 911 covers ambulance, fire and police services nationally. Mexico City Tourist Police: (0052) 55 5207 4155.
mx-emergency-ambulance.title: Single emergency number: 911 (ambulance, fire, police)

mx-entry-fees.content: Quintana Roo state charges an entry tax (payable online or at the airport). A departure tax may apply when leaving by air or land depending on location.
mx-entry-fees.title: Quintana Roo entry tax and possible departure tax

mx-entry-passport.content: Passport must be valid for the duration of stay; the Mexican Embassy recommends at least 180 days' validity (the maximum tourist stay length). Onward transit through other countries may require 6 months' validity.
mx-entry-passport.title: Passport valid for stay; 180 days recommended

mx-entry-visa.content: No visa is needed for tourist visits by British citizens; a passport stamp indicates the allowed stay. Entry by land requires completion of an online immigration form via the INM website beforehand. Work or study requires a visa arranged before travel.
mx-entry-visa.title: No visa needed for tourism; land entrants must file online form

mx-health-quality.content: Outside state capitals and larger urban areas, medical and emergency services may be limited. Many hospitals do not work directly with insurance and require upfront payment.
mx-health-quality.title: Limited outside major cities; upfront payment often required

mx-health-risks.content: Health risks include Zika virus, chikungunya, dengue, and air pollution; altitude sickness is a risk in certain regions.
mx-health-risks.title: Zika, chikungunya, dengue and air pollution

mx-health-water.content: Only boiled or bottled water should be consumed and ice in drinks avoided, to prevent waterborne illness including Cyclospora.
mx-health-water.title: Boiled/bottled water recommended

mx-security-acapulco.content: The FCDO advises against all but essential travel to the city of Acapulco due to infrastructure damage from Hurricane Otis (2023) and unpredictable security.
mx-security-acapulco.title: Acapulco: all but essential travel advised against

mx-security-crime.content: Drug-related violence has escalated, including gang-related shootings in tourist zones such as Cancun. Express kidnappings (forcing victims to withdraw ATM funds) occur in urban areas; longer-term kidnappings also happen. Impersonators posing as police demand bribes.
mx-security-crime.title: Drug-related violence and express kidnapping risk

mx-security-driving.content: Driving standards differ significantly from UK norms with potholes and unpredictable conditions; many drivers lack insurance. Avoid isolated roads and use toll roads where possible; vehicle hijackings reported along the Pacific Highway.
mx-security-driving.title: Poor conditions; avoid isolated roads, use toll roads

mx-security-terrorism.content: There is a high threat of terrorist attack globally affecting UK interests and British nationals; attacks in Mexico cannot be ruled out.
mx-security-terrorism.title: Terrorist attacks cannot be ruled out

ng-emergency-general.notes: No dedicated national ambulance service — see Health category.
ng-emergency-general.title: General emergency number: 112

ng-entry-passport.content: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your arrival date.
ng-entry-passport.title: Passport must be valid at least 6 months beyond arrival

ng-entry-visa.content: A visa is mandatory and must be obtained before departure via the online Nigerian Immigration Services portal; visa on arrival is no longer available. Valid CERPAC/Green Card residence-permit holders are exempt.
ng-entry-visa.title: Visa required in advance — visa on arrival no longer available

ng-entry-yellowfever.content: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required (exemptions for infants under 8 months and adults 61+), plus an online Nigeria Health Declaration Form before entry. Enhanced screening may apply for arrivals from East/Central Africa.
ng-entry-yellowfever.title: Yellow fever certificate and health declaration required

ng-health-ambulance.content: There is no national ambulance service and hospital ambulances are severely restricted; you may need to arrange local transport. General emergency number: 112.
ng-health-ambulance.title: No national ambulance service

ng-health-quality.content: Medical standards differ significantly from the UK. Public hospitals require payment and private facilities are considerably more expensive, with possible overcrowding and equipment shortages.
ng-health-quality.title: Standards vary; public hospitals require payment upfront

ng-security-crime.content: High levels of violent street crime include armed robbery and carjackings, with British nationals sometimes targeted as perceived wealthy. Criminal groups run illegal checkpoints on major highways, notably the Abuja-Kaduna route.
ng-security-crime.title: High levels of armed robbery and carjacking; illegal checkpoints

ng-security-kidnap.content: Kidnappings are widespread and could occur anywhere in Nigeria, affecting foreign nationals, aid workers and tourists. Criminal kidnap is particularly severe in the northwest (Zamfara, Katsina, Kaduna) and central states. The Niger Delta's oil and gas facilities — including offshore installations — face a high threat of kidnapping and other armed attacks; oil and gas workers should treat this as a heightened, ongoing risk.
ng-security-kidnap.title: Kidnapping widespread and could occur anywhere

ng-security-terrorism.content: Terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Nigeria. The primary threat is from ISWA and Boko Haram, based mainly in Borno, Yobe and Adamawa states, though attacks have occurred more widely. Targets include places of worship, markets, hotels and public gatherings.
ng-security-terrorism.title: Very likely terrorism risk, concentrated in the northeast

no-entry-passport.content: Your passport must have been issued less than 10 years before your arrival date, and have an expiry date at least 3 months after you plan to leave the Schengen area.
no-entry-passport.title: Passport must meet Schengen age/validity rules

no-entry-visa.content: British citizens can enter visa-free for tourism, family visits or short study for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, calculated across the whole Schengen area. Overstaying risks a Schengen ban of up to 3 years.
no-entry-visa.title: Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period

no-health-access.content: UK nationals can access state-provided hospital treatment using their passport, though some doctors may charge separately. A GHIC or EHIC card is not an alternative to full travel insurance.
no-health-access.title: State hospital treatment accessible with passport; GHIC/EHIC not a substitute for insurance

no-security-arctic.content: Nearly half of Norway lies within the Arctic Circle. In these extremely isolated regions, emergency medical assistance and search and rescue are limited, and winter temperatures can fall to -25°C and below with severe wind chill.
no-security-arctic.notes: Relevant for any North Sea / Arctic oil & gas site travel.
no-security-arctic.title: Arctic areas have limited emergency response

no-security-avalanche.content: Avalanche season extends well into April, with associated flood and landslide risk in mountainous and exposed areas; weather can shift rapidly even in summer at high elevations.
no-security-avalanche.title: Avalanche, flood and landslide risk into spring

no-security-terrorism.content: Terrorist attacks in Norway cannot be ruled out, in line with a global high threat level affecting UK interests and nationals.
no-security-terrorism.title: Terrorist attacks cannot be ruled out

om-emergency-ambulance.content: Call 9999 and ask for an ambulance.
om-emergency-ambulance.title: Ambulance emergency number: 9999

om-entry-dualnational.content: British-Omani dual nationals should note Oman does not recognise dual citizenship; authorities may confiscate one passport.
om-entry-dualnational.title: Oman does not recognise dual citizenship

om-entry-passport.content: Your passport must remain valid for at least 6 months beyond your arrival date in Oman.
om-entry-passport.title: Passport must be valid at least 6 months beyond arrival

om-entry-visa.content: British citizens can enter visa-free for stays up to 14 days. Longer stays or non-tourism purposes need an advance e-visa (apply online rather than on arrival to reduce rejection risk). Overstay penalties run up to 10 OMR/day, max 500 OMR, plus possible detention.
om-entry-visa.title: Visa-free for 14 days; e-visa recommended for longer stays

om-health-quality.content: Healthcare facilities are comparable to UK standards, but British nationals must use the private healthcare system. Travellers without adequate insurance or funds may be prevented from leaving Oman until bills are settled.
om-health-quality.title: Good standard but private-only for British nationals

om-security-driving.content: Road accident rates are significantly higher than UK standards, with wandering livestock and flash-flood-prone wadis outside Muscat. Desert travel requires well-equipped vehicles and, where possible, convoy travel.
om-security-driving.title: Higher accident rates; hazards outside Muscat

om-security-lawsculture.content: Oman enforces strict Islamic law: public alcohol consumption or being intoxicated at airports, e-cigarettes/vapes (banned outright), unmarried cohabitation, and same-sex relations are all illegal, with drug possession carrying severe penalties including potential death sentence.
om-security-lawsculture.title: Strict Islamic law — alcohol, vaping, cohabitation, same-sex relations

om-security-terrorism.content: Terrorist attacks in Oman cannot be ruled out and could target residential compounds, military, oil, transport and aviation interests, as well as restaurants, hotels, beaches, shopping centres and places of worship. A July 2024 shooting near a mosque in Muscat killed six people.
om-security-terrorism.title: Terrorist attacks cannot be ruled out

qa-entry-passport.content: As a visitor, your passport must be valid for at least 6 months from the date you arrive.
qa-entry-passport.title: Passport must be valid at least 6 months for visitors

qa-entry-transit.content: Transit passengers face strict drug policy — even residual/trace amounts can lead to arrest — and transit stays cannot exceed 24 hours.
qa-entry-transit.title: Transit passengers face strict drug policy, 24-hour limit

qa-entry-visa.content: Full British citizen passport holders can get a tourist visa on arrival; other passport types or non-tourism purposes need to apply in advance. Stays over 30 days require an extension via the Ministry of Interior before expiry.
qa-entry-visa.title: Tourist visa on arrival for full British citizen passport holders

qa-health-quality.content: Healthcare facilities are similar to the UK, but visitors must pay for treatment — comprehensive travel health insurance with adequate coverage is essential.
qa-health-quality.title: Similar standard to the UK but payment required

qa-security-laws.content: Public drinking can mean up to 6 months' imprisonment; unmarried cohabitation, sex outside marriage and same-sex relations are illegal; drug possession has zero tolerance; photographing people without consent can mean imprisonment or fines up to 100,000 QAR; e-cigarettes are criminalised.
qa-security-laws.title: Severe penalties for alcohol, relationships, drugs, vaping, photography

qa-security-terrorism.content: Terrorist attacks in Qatar cannot be ruled out, with threats specifically mentioning Western interests including hotels, restaurants and shopping centres.
qa-security-terrorism.title: Attacks cannot be ruled out; Western-linked venues flagged

ru-emergency-ambulance.content: Dial 112 and ask for an ambulance.
ru-emergency-ambulance.title: Emergency number: 112

ru-entry-visa.content: A visa is required before travel, applied for in person at a visa application centre (London, Manchester or Edinburgh) to provide biometric data. This is only relevant to travellers who choose to go against FCDO advice.
ru-entry-visa.notes: The FCDO advises against all travel — see the SECURITY category.
ru-entry-visa.title: Visa required in advance despite FCDO advising against all travel

ru-health-quality.content: Medical care in Russia may not meet Western standards. Hospitals may request payment before treatment, and in remote regions may not use disposable IV supplies/syringes/needles as standard practice.
ru-health-quality.title: May not meet Western standards; bring own medical supplies in remote areas

ru-security-advisory.content: The FCDO advises against all travel to Russia. This reflects the ongoing war with Ukraine (drone attacks and explosions near the border and in major cities), heightened terrorism risk, and a legal environment in which foreigners can face lengthy imprisonment on limited grounds, with extremely limited UK consular ability to assist.
ru-security-advisory.notes: Fast-changing — review at least monthly given the conflict.
ru-security-advisory.title: FCDO advises against all travel to Russia

ru-security-detention.content: Since December 2024 Russia has expanded liability for foreigners suspected of acting against Russian interests (e.g. displaying LGBT+ symbols, expressing support for Ukraine online). Dual British-Russian nationals are especially vulnerable, as Russian authorities may deny UK consular access to detainees.
ru-security-detention.title: Expanded legal risk for foreigners, especially dual nationals

ru-security-terrorism.content: Terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Russia — the March 2024 Crocus City Hall attack near Moscow killed 145 people. Large gatherings, concerts and popular tourist sites are considered at risk.
ru-security-terrorism.title: Terrorists very likely to try to carry out attacks

sa-emergency-ambulance.content: Saudi Red Crescent Authority ambulance emergency number: 997.
sa-emergency-ambulance.title: Ambulance emergency number: 997

sa-emergency-fire.content: Civil defence and fire emergency number: 998.
sa-emergency-fire.title: Civil defence / fire emergency number: 998

sa-emergency-police.notes: Cross-check locally; numbering has changed in some regions in recent years.
sa-emergency-police.title: Police emergency number: 911

sa-entry-israel.content: You may not be allowed to enter Saudi Arabia if your passport shows that you have travelled to, or were born in, Israel.
sa-entry-israel.title: Entry may be refused for prior travel to, or birth in, Israel

sa-entry-passport.content: Your passport must remain valid for at least 6 months beyond your arrival date in Saudi Arabia. You will not be permitted entry if your passport has been reported lost or stolen.
sa-entry-passport.notes: Stated for British nationals; verify equivalent rule for other nationalities.
sa-entry-passport.title: Passport must be valid at least 6 months beyond arrival

sa-entry-transit.content: A transit visa is required if you will pass through Saudi immigration, are travelling on separate tickets, or have a layover exceeding 12 hours. Overland travellers via the Bahrain causeway should verify their visa permits that route.
sa-entry-transit.title: Transit visa needed for some layovers

sa-entry-visa.content: A visa is required. Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA): tourism, business, study, medical treatment or Umrah outside Hajj season; valid 730 days, multiple entries, 180 days total, no health insurance included. E-Visa: tourists only; valid 365 days, multiple entries, 90 days total, includes health insurance cover up to 100,000 SAR. Electronic Visa Waiver: tourism, business, medical treatment, study or Umrah; single entry, up to 180 days, apply 48 hours to 90 days before travel, no health insurance included.
sa-entry-visa.notes: Stated for British nationals — requirements vary by nationality.
sa-entry-visa.title: Visa required — three route options depending on purpose

sa-health-hajj-heat.content: Heat stroke and dehydration are a real risk during the summer months. Contagious diseases can spread rapidly, particularly during Hajj and Ramadan when very large crowds gather.
sa-health-hajj-heat.title: Heat, dehydration and contagious disease risk

sa-health-medication.content: Some UK prescription and over-the-counter medicines are controlled substances in Saudi Arabia. If you need to bring medication, carry official documentation from your doctor stating the amount prescribed and drug/dosage details. A UK prescription is not valid locally — only a Saudi-licensed doctor can issue a prescription there.
sa-health-medication.title: Some UK medicines are controlled substances in Saudi Arabia

sa-health-quality.content: Healthcare facilities in major Saudi cities are of a high standard. Most towns have health centres or basic hospitals, though serious cases may require transfer to a major city.
