sa-health-quality.title: High-standard healthcare in major cities

sa-health-vaccinations.content: Check the latest vaccine recommendations for Saudi Arabia at least 8 weeks before travel via TravelHealthPro or the NHS travel vaccinations service. Proof of yellow fever vaccination is required if arriving from an endemic area, and the meningococcal quadrivalent vaccine is required for Hajj/Umrah pilgrims.
sa-health-vaccinations.title: Check current vaccine recommendations before travel

sa-security-facilities.content: Avoid the vicinity of security and military facilities, which have been targeted in the past. Travel insurance may be invalidated if you travel against FCDO advice, so check your policy against the current advice before travelling.
sa-security-facilities.title: Stay away from security and military facilities

sa-security-regional-tension.content: There is a risk of escalating Middle East conflict, including strikes and retaliatory attacks involving Iran, and Houthi attacks on Saudi territory and infrastructure since mid-July 2026. The Houthis have launched missiles and drones targeting multiple Saudi cities, airports, and military/energy sites, including Riyadh, Jeddah, Abha, Jizan, Najran and Yanbu, and could do so again at short notice. Expect possible flight cancellations and periodic airspace closures, and avoid the vicinity of military and energy infrastructure.
sa-security-regional-tension.title: Risk of regional escalation, including Houthi attacks

sa-security-yemen-border.content: The FCDO advises against all travel within 10km of the Saudi–Yemen border, and against all but essential travel between 10–80km of it, due to the ongoing regional conflict. This zone has been expanded to include the cities of Abha and Khamis Mushait in Aseer province.
sa-security-yemen-border.title: Avoid all travel within 10km of the Yemen border

tm-emergency-ambulance.content: Ambulance: 03 from landline, 003 from mobile. Fire: 01 landline / 001 mobile. Police: 02 landline / 002 mobile.
tm-emergency-ambulance.title: Ambulance: 03 (landline) / 003 (mobile)

tm-entry-currency.content: Turkmenistan operates primarily on cash (manat); USD and EUR exchange easily at official rates but bring clean, new bills. ATMs in Ashgabat charge 3% per withdrawal. Manat cannot be reconverted to foreign currency, and export of manat is restricted.
tm-entry-currency.notes: Operationally significant for any personnel travel — arrange cash logistics before travel.
tm-entry-currency.title: Cash-based economy; manat cannot be reconverted

tm-entry-passport.content: Passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after the planned departure date from Turkmenistan.
tm-entry-passport.title: Passport valid 6 months beyond planned departure

tm-entry-registration.content: Registration is required if staying over 3 working days, typically handled by hotels or sponsors. A migration fee ($14 USD) and daily tourism tax ($2 USD) apply.
tm-entry-registration.title: Registration required for stays over 3 working days

tm-entry-visa.content: All visitors need a visa and a letter of invitation obtained beforehand (via a travel agent for tourism, or a company/ministry letter for business). Embassy applications take up to one month; visas on arrival are available at Ashgabat International Airport and select land borders. Transit visas (under 5 days) cannot be converted to tourist visas.
tm-entry-visa.title: Visa mandatory; letter of invitation required

tm-health-quality.content: The quality of medical care is poor and considerably more expensive than in the UK. Basic or emergency services outside the capital are best avoided. There is no reciprocal healthcare agreement with the UK.
tm-health-quality.title: Poor quality and expensive; no reciprocal agreement

tm-health-risks.content: Typhoid and hepatitis A are endemic. Summer temperatures regularly exceed 45°C, requiring hydration and sun protection. Air quality in cities fluctuates periodically.
tm-health-risks.notes: Extreme summer heat directly relevant to any outdoor gas-field work.
tm-health-risks.title: Typhoid, hepatitis A, extreme summer heat

tm-health-water.content: Drink or use only boiled and filtered or bottled water and avoid ice in drinks.
tm-health-water.title: Only boiled/filtered or bottled water recommended

tm-security-driving.content: Driving conditions are hazardous outside urban areas, particularly at night, due to poor road conditions. Ashgabat enforces a 60 km/h speed limit via unmarked cameras. Use only licensed (white/green marked) taxis.
tm-security-driving.title: Hazardous outside urban areas at night

tm-security-laws.content: VPNs are illegal and blocked. Negative political commentary on social media is treated as an offence. Alcohol consumption in public spaces carries 100-manat fines; drug possession results in lengthy prison sentences under basic conditions. Male same-sex activity is criminalised.
tm-security-laws.title: VPNs illegal; strict alcohol and speech rules

tm-security-restrictions.content: Border areas near Afghanistan and Iran are tightly restricted with occasional unannounced closures. Photography of airports, military sites, police stations, government buildings and embassies is prohibited without permission.
tm-security-restrictions.notes: Relevant for any gas-field travel near restricted border zones.
tm-security-restrictions.title: Border areas restricted; photography of official sites banned

tm-security-terrorism.content: Although there is no recent history of terrorism in Turkmenistan, attacks cannot be ruled out given the broader global terrorism threat affecting British interests.
tm-security-terrorism.title: No recent history but attacks cannot be ruled out

us-emergency-ambulance.content: Dial 911 and ask for an ambulance.
us-emergency-ambulance.title: Emergency number: 911

us-entry-esta.content: Travellers need either an approved ESTA (Visa Waiver Program) or a US visa before arrival — a valid ESTA/visa does not guarantee entry. You cannot use ESTA if you have prior arrests/convictions, were previously deported or refused entry, overstayed a past ESTA, or have travelled to Iran, Iraq, Libya, North Korea, Somalia, Sudan, Syria or Yemen since March 2011, or Cuba since 12 Jan 2021.
us-entry-esta.notes: Relevant for oil & gas travellers with Middle East travel history — check ESTA eligibility carefully.
us-entry-esta.title: ESTA or visa required before travel; ineligibility triggers

us-entry-passport.content: Your passport must be valid for the length of your planned stay in the US; many transit countries separately require 6 months' remaining validity.
us-entry-passport.title: Passport must be valid for the length of stay

us-health-cost.content: Medical treatment is expensive and there are no special arrangements for British visitors; some hospitals require deposits from non-residents. Comprehensive travel health insurance is essential.
us-health-cost.title: Medical treatment is expensive with no special arrangements for visitors

us-security-borderareas.content: Crime linked to illegal drugs is significant in Mexican border areas of Arizona, California, New Mexico and Texas, though foreign nationals are not specifically targeted.
us-security-borderareas.title: Drug-related crime near the Mexican border

us-security-naturaldisaster.content: Hurricane season runs June-November (Atlantic) and May-November (Pacific). Wildfires are prevalent in dry areas; earthquake risk is higher in Alaska, California, Hawaii, Oregon, Washington and Puerto Rico; tornadoes and flash floods can occur with minimal warning.
us-security-naturaldisaster.title: Hurricanes, wildfires, tornadoes and earthquakes by region

us-security-terrorism.content: Terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in the US, with potential targets including crowded venues, transport hubs, sporting events and religious sites.
us-security-terrorism.title: Terrorists very likely to try to carry out attacks

ve-emergency-ambulance.content: 911 covers ambulance, fire and police services.
ve-emergency-ambulance.title: Single emergency number: 911 (ambulance, fire, police)

ve-entry-currency.content: Goods worth over $1,000 USD and cash/traveller's cheques of $10,000 USD or more must be declared on entry; import tax applies to new-looking items.
ve-entry-currency.title: Declare goods over $1,000 and cash over $10,000

ve-entry-dualnational.content: Venezuelan dual nationals must use Venezuelan identity documents for entry and exit; departure may be denied without a valid Venezuelan passport.
ve-entry-dualnational.title: Venezuelan dual nationals must use Venezuelan documents

ve-entry-passport.content: Passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond the planned departure date. Entry is denied if the document is reported lost or stolen.
ve-entry-passport.title: Passport valid 6 months beyond departure

ve-entry-visa.content: Arrival by air allows a stay of up to 90 days visa-free on a tourist card issued on arrival, with a return/onward ticket required. Arrival overland or by sea may require an advance visa. Tourist cards can be extended up to 90 more days via SAIME. Work, NGO, journalism or study activities require an advance visa.
ve-entry-visa.title: Visa-free tourist card for up to 90 days by air

ve-health-medication.content: The Venezuelan Pharmaceutical Federation has reported an 80% shortage of medical supplies due to the economic crisis. Travellers must bring sufficient medication for their entire stay, plus extra in case of delayed return.
ve-health-medication.title: Severe medicine shortages — bring a full supply plus extra

ve-health-quality.content: Private clinics in major cities offer acceptable care for routine treatment but face acute shortages of medical supplies and medicines. Public facilities are poor with chronic shortages. Comprehensive treatment may require medical evacuation.
ve-health-quality.title: Public facilities poor; medicine shortages acute

ve-health-risks.content: Health risks include yellow fever, dengue fever, schistosomiasis, and altitude sickness (particularly in Mérida, Táchira and Trujillo states).
ve-health-risks.title: Yellow fever, dengue, schistosomiasis

ve-security-crime.content: Armed robbery, mugging, carjacking and burglary are prevalent and often violent. Use only pre-booked taxis from reputable companies; do not resist an attacker. High-risk areas include Zulia, Táchira, Apure states, and the Orinoco Mining Arc.
ve-security-crime.notes: Zulia state borders Lake Maracaibo's oil operations — directly relevant to any oil & gas travel.
ve-security-crime.title: Armed robbery and carjacking prevalent and often violent

ve-security-detention.content: Some foreign nationals, including Europeans, have been detained and accused of terrorism. Support from the FCDO to detained British nationals may be severely limited.
ve-security-detention.title: Foreign nationals detained and accused of terrorism

ve-security-noall.content: The FCDO advises against all travel to parts of Venezuela and against all but essential travel to other parts.
ve-security-noall.notes: Fast-changing — review at least monthly given the unstable political situation.
ve-security-noall.title: FCDO advises against all/essential travel to parts of Venezuela

ve-security-political.content: The UK does not recognise the current Venezuelan administration. Military presence is visible in major cities and consular access/support to British nationals may be severely limited. A 'state of external commotion' was declared on 3 January due to airstrikes. Following earthquakes on 24 June 2026 (magnitudes 7.2 and 7.5), La Guaira state — home to Venezuela's main international airport — was declared a disaster zone under military control with strict access restrictions.
ve-security-political.title: UK does not recognise current administration; consular support limited

bh-entry-travel-ban.content: Travellers involved in legal disputes, custody matters, or with unpaid debts may be subject to a travel ban that can become apparent only when attempting to leave the country.
bh-entry-travel-ban.title: Possible undisclosed exit/travel bans from legal or debt disputes

bh-entry-visa.content: A visa is required; the standard tourist visa is issued automatically for two weeks (longer stays of up to six months are available), obtainable online in advance (e-visa), from the Bahraini Embassy in the UK, or on arrival. Passports must be valid for at least 6 months after the date of arrival.
bh-entry-visa.title: Visa on arrival or e-visa available

bh-security-laws.content: Photographing security or military sites is prohibited and risks arrest and prosecution. Social media posts critical of the government or monarchy are treated as criminal activity. Public intoxication and drug possession carry severe penalties, including potential life sentences for trafficking, and disrespect toward Islam can result in a heavy fine or imprisonment.
bh-security-laws.title: Strict laws on photography, speech, alcohol and drugs

bh-security-protests.content: Protests and demonstrations occur regularly and can disrupt traffic and cause localised clashes between security forces and protesters; risk increases around anniversaries of significant events in Bahrain. The government has temporarily banned large public gatherings on roads and in squares. Leave the area if a large public gathering or demonstration is seen.
bh-security-protests.title: Regular protests, risk rises around anniversaries

bh-security-terrorism.content: Terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Bahrain, which could be indiscriminate and target places visited by foreigners including residential compounds, oil and transport infrastructure, restaurants, hotels, beaches, shopping centres and mosques — though no attack has been carried out successfully for several years.
bh-security-terrorism.title: Terrorism likely but no successful attack in recent years

il-entry-eta.content: Since 1 January 2025, an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) is required before arrival, valid for 2 years and covering visits of up to 90 days; the ETA costs 25 new Israeli shekels and is applied for via the Israel Population and Immigration Authority. Passports must be valid for at least 90 days beyond the arrival date.
il-entry-eta.title: Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) required since Jan 2025

il-entry-refusal.content: Entry may be refused to those who have publicly called for a boycott of Israel or Israeli settlements, belong to an organisation that has, or have publicly denied the Holocaust or the 7 October 2023 attack.
il-entry-refusal.title: Grounds for entry refusal beyond standard requirements

il-security-advice.content: The FCDO advises against all travel to Gaza and against all but essential travel to parts of Israel, including areas near the Lebanon border (a cessation of hostilities between Israel and Lebanese Hizballah was announced on 16 April 2026, though fighting continues intermittently and hostilities could reignite with little warning) and near the Egypt border (kidnap risk).
il-security-advice.title: Advises against travel to Gaza and parts of Israel

il-security-rockets.content: Rocket, drone and missile fire (including from Houthi forces in Yemen) poses a risk throughout Israel, including from interception debris; Ben Gurion Airport can face disruption. Two Houthi drones fell in Eilat in September 2025, injuring at least 20 people.
il-security-rockets.title: Rocket, drone and missile risk nationwide

il-security-terrorism.content: Terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Israel and Palestine, with an increased threat of attacks including by individuals acting alone. Recent incidents include a September 2025 shooting in northern Jerusalem (six killed, eight wounded), bomb discoveries on Tel Aviv buses in February 2025, and multiple stabbing/ramming attacks.
il-security-terrorism.title: Very likely terrorist attacks, including lone-actor risk

sy-entry-advice-against.content: The FCDO advises against all travel to Syria, making the published entry requirements largely theoretical; rules should be verified directly with Syrian authorities given the ongoing political transition.
sy-entry-advice-against.title: FCDO advises against all travel to Syria

sy-entry-visa.content: A visa is mandatory, applied for online, typically taking approximately 5-7 days to process though this can vary; passports must be valid for at least 3 months after the date of arrival. Israeli and Iranian citizens cannot enter, and travellers with Israeli stamps in their passport may be refused entry.
sy-entry-visa.title: Visa mandatory; entry barred for Israeli/Iranian citizens

sy-security-kidnap.content: There is a very high threat of kidnapping from terrorists throughout Syria, including Al-Qaeda-affiliated groups and Daesh. British nationals are explicitly targeted and some hostages have been killed.
sy-security-kidnap.title: Very high kidnap threat; British nationals targeted

sy-security-ordnance.content: Landmines and other unexploded ordnance remain from the Syrian conflict, with particular risk in less populated and rural areas and near former conflict lines.
sy-security-ordnance.title: Landmine and unexploded ordnance risk

sy-security-terrorism.content: Terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Syria. Daesh continues to carry out regular attacks nationwide, including in Damascus — recent incidents include an explosives attack on the Four Seasons hotel and Tourism Ministry (7 July 2026, 1 killed, 36 injured), a café bombing in central Damascus (2 July 2026, 9 killed, 22 injured), and an attack on a Greek Orthodox church (2 June 2025, at least 30 killed).
sy-security-terrorism.title: Regular Daesh attacks nationwide, including Damascus

sy-security-transition.content: The security situation remains volatile following the fall of the Assad government; fighting and violence may occur around the country. Some areas, particularly Suwayda province, are controlled by local armed groups rather than the Syrian government.
sy-security-transition.title: Volatile situation post-Assad; some areas outside government control

ye-entry-advice-against.content: The FCDO advises against all travel to Yemen; the published entry requirements apply only to those who choose to travel against that advice.
ye-entry-advice-against.title: FCDO advises against all travel to Yemen

ye-entry-visa.content: A visa is required and must be obtained from the Yemeni Embassy in the UK before travel — there is no visa on arrival. Passports must be valid for at least 6 months after the date of arrival. Stays of more than two weeks require registration with Yemen's immigration authorities after arrival.
ye-entry-visa.title: Visa required in advance; no visa on arrival

ye-security-conflict.content: A de facto ceasefire between the Houthis and the Yemeni government has held since April 2022, formalised by a UN-announced commitment on 23 December 2023, but sporadic incidents continue along frontlines and the security situation remains volatile. Following US/UK airstrikes in February 2026, the Houthis formally designated the US and UK as hostile states, escalating the threat level; large-scale conflict could resume without warning.
ye-security-conflict.title: De facto ceasefire holding but volatile since Apr 2022

ye-security-houthi.content: Travel to Houthi-controlled areas is strongly advised against. Red Sea shipping faces an ongoing risk from Houthi forces due to the potential for misidentification.
ye-security-houthi.title: Avoid Houthi-controlled areas; Red Sea shipping risk

ye-security-kidnap.content: There is a very high and constant threat of kidnap across Yemen. AQAP has called for continued kidnapping of Westerners, and criminal groups may sell hostages to terrorist organisations.
ye-security-kidnap.title: Very high, constant kidnap threat

ye-security-landmines.content: Landmines from the current and previous conflicts are a risk on Yemen's roads.
ye-security-landmines.title: Landmine risk on roads

ye-security-terrorism.content: Terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Yemen. Al-Qaida in the Arabian Peninsula (AQAP) and Islamic State-Yemen pose a heightened threat in Abyan, Marib, Hadramawt and Shabwah governorates, using bombings, assassinations and suicide attacks against hotels, airports, transport routes and government buildings.
ye-security-terrorism.title: Very likely terrorist attacks, heightened in four governorates
